newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials bounce firmer on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials bounce firmer on U.S. data.

text.p: Life was breathed into South African industrial shares shortly before the close of trade on Tuesday after stocks had held in weaker territory for the best part of the day after falls on Wall Street on Monday night.

Dealers said expectations of a stronger Dow Jones index on Tuesday swept the local market following the release of a lower than forecast rise in the fourth quarter U.S. employment cost index -- an indicator closely watched by the Federal Reserve.

Industrials almost stole the limelight from gold shares which after a day of strong gains on the back of a more robust bullion price, slipped off their best levels as the metal once again edged below the $356 an ounce level.
The gold index ended firmly in the red, up 3.93 percent or 54.1 points to 1,429.4.
Dealers were optimistic about gains on Wednesday on the expected U.S. market gains and helped by a more buoyant rand and long bond market.
The industrial ended 25.1 points firmer at 8,069.0, which together with gold stock gains lifted the overall market index by 47.0 points to 6,736.4.
